content:
Shopify lets a brand start selling without worrying about servers, updates or security patches. That is why many young D2C brands in Gurugram, selling apparel, skincare, home decor or packaged food, choose it. But a Shopify store set up with default settings is not ready for Indian buyers. Payments, COD, GST, shipping and speed all need attention. We set up, customise and migrate Shopify stores from our office on Sohna Road, and this page explains what that involves.

Is Shopify the right platform for you?

Shopify fits well if

  • You sell physical products to consumers and want to launch in weeks, not months.
  • You would rather pay a monthly subscription than manage hosting, updates and security.
  • Your team is non-technical and needs a simple admin panel for products, orders and discounts.
  • You plan to grow through Instagram, Meta and Google ads, and want solid tracking and catalogue sync.

Look at other options if

  • You need complex B2B pricing, dealer-specific catalogues or credit terms. WooCommerce or a custom build may cost less over time.
  • Your products are mainly services, bookings or course enrolments.
  • You want total control over URLs and server behaviour. Shopify uses set URL patterns, such as /products/ and /collections/, that cannot be changed.
  • Monthly app subscriptions, many billed in US dollars, would strain your budget.

Making Shopify work for Indian buyers

Most of our Shopify work is here, rather than in the design:

  • Payments. We connect an Indian gateway such as Razorpay, PayU or Cashfree so buyers can pay by UPI, cards, net banking and wallets, and we test the full flow including failed and refunded payments.
  • Cash on delivery. Set up as a manual payment method, with rules or apps to limit it by order value or pincode and to confirm COD orders before dispatch.
  • GST. Tax-inclusive pricing configured correctly, HSN codes added to products, and a GST invoice app so each order produces a compliant invoice.
  • Shipping. Integration with Shiprocket or Delhivery for labels, pickups and tracking, plus a pincode checker on product pages.
  • Order updates. Confirmation and shipping messages on WhatsApp as well as email, since many buyers check WhatsApp first.

Theme choice: free, premium or custom

Every Online Store 2.0 theme, including Shopify's free Dawn theme, lets you rearrange sections without code. For many new brands, a well-chosen theme with custom styling and a few custom Liquid sections is enough, and it keeps costs and load times down. A premium theme from the Shopify Theme Store adds ready-made features for a one-time licence fee. A fully custom theme makes sense when your brand needs layouts or product experiences that no theme offers, such as a build-your-own gift box or a detailed size guide per product type. We show you options side by side and explain what each one changes.

Apps we commonly work with

  • Razorpay
  • Cashfree
  • Shiprocket
  • Delhivery
  • Judge.me reviews
  • Shopify Search & Discovery
  • Shopify Email
  • Google & YouTube channel
  • Facebook & Instagram channel

Every app adds scripts that can slow your store. We install only what you need and remove leftover code when an app is uninstalled.

From sign-up to first order

  1. Store set-up (week 1): Shopify account in your name, plan selection, domain connection, taxes, shipping zones and policies.
  2. Theme and design (weeks 1 to 3): home, collection and product page designs, then theme customisation.
  3. Products and collections (weeks 2 to 3): bulk import from your spreadsheet, variants, images, filters and SEO fields.
  4. Payments, shipping and apps (weeks 3 to 4): gateway, COD rules, courier integration, invoices and notifications.
  5. Test orders and launch (week 4 or 5): real orders on every payment method, then removing the store password.

A store with a ready product list usually goes live in 3 to 5 weeks. A fully custom theme or a migration adds time.

Moving from WooCommerce or another platform

We migrate products, customers and past orders, then rebuild navigation and collections. Because Shopify uses its own URL structure, every old product and category URL is redirected to its new address so your search rankings and ad links keep working. Customer passwords cannot be carried across, so we plan an account re-activation email for your existing buyers.

What you need to provide

A product sheet with titles, prices, variants, weights and HSN codes; product and lifestyle photos; your logo and brand guidelines; business documents for gateway KYC; and written return and shipping policies. You also need to add your own payment method to the Shopify account, since the subscription is billed to you.

Running costs to plan for

We give a fixed quote for our work after a free consultation. Separately, budget for the Shopify plan, any transaction fees Shopify charges on your plan, your payment gateway's charges, monthly app subscriptions and a premium theme licence if you choose one. We list all of these in writing before you commit, so the monthly bill holds no surprises.

What we check before your store goes live

  • Mobile PageSpeed and Core Web Vitals on the home, collection and product pages.
  • Checkout tested on UPI, cards and COD on a real phone over mobile data.
  • GST invoice output checked for orders within Haryana and outside it.
  • Staff accounts with only the permissions each person needs, and two-step login switched on.
  • Google Analytics, Search Console and Meta pixel events firing correctly.

Shopify questions we hear often

Do I own my Shopify store?

Yes. The store is opened under your email and billing, and we work as staff or collaborators. You can remove our access at any time.

Can I offer cash on delivery on Shopify?

Yes. COD is a built-in manual payment option, and we add rules to limit it by order value or pincode, plus a confirmation step to cut down on fake orders.

Can Shopify generate GST invoices?

Yes, through an invoice app configured with your GSTIN, HSN codes and state-wise tax split. We recommend your accountant checks a few sample invoices before launch.

Will my store be slow because of apps?

It can be if apps pile up. We keep the app list short, test speed after each one, and clean up code left behind by old apps.

Can you work on a Shopify store someone else built?

Yes. We start by reviewing the theme, apps and settings, then fix the most costly issues first.
